static_traits.name: Chen Cody
static_traits.social_status: has supportive friends and family, but has not yet discussed these specific feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received before; no similar problem experiences yet
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation; thinking tends to be rigid, often uses 'must/should' style rules; easily self-blaming and self-labeling; cautious tone, concerned about moral consistency.

basic_info.main_problem: after accidentally eating meat-containing food once, I fell into guilt and anxiety, believing I am a terrible vegan.
basic_info.core_demands: guilt and anxiety affect my daily life and focus on building the online business, hoping to ease these feelings.

core_beliefs: Must be absolutely perfect to qualify

special_situations.event: After a dinner with friends, learned that the dish eaten contained meat
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I make one mistake as a vegan, it proves I am unqualified/a bad vegan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: doubling down on vegan-related research, constantly reminding oneself of values, imposing stricter self-Demands to avoid mistakes again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not make such mistakes; I am a terrible vegan

special_situations.event: When beginning to focus on work or the online business, guilt repeatedly intrudes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I cannot achieve absolute perfection, it equals failure, unable to focus on Work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: excessive Self-monitoring and rumination, trying to drive oneself to be more careful through self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I failed again, I do not deserve to relax or focus

special_situations.event: When dining out or socializing with others, worries about mistakes related to vegan living
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: if I make a mistake in social dining situations, I will be seen as not a true vegan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication on this topic and chooses food and settings even more cautiously
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may make mistakes again and lose face in front of others

special_situations.event: Repeatedly recalling the accidental-ingestion incident afterwards
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake can fully define who I am
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: constantly blaming oneself in an attempt to make up for the fault
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This one time is enough to show I am a bad vegan

core_conflict.wish: longing to fully comply with vegan values and be seen as morally consistent, a flawless person
core_conflict.fear: fear of being negated as hypocritical or unqualified by one mistake, losing self-worth and others' approval
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and purity through strict rules and self-criticism
Avoids talking to others about this feeling to evade outside judgment

object_relations.self_representation: an unqualified vegan with a stain

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: when the counselor proposes turning rigid 'must/cannot' rules into more flexible 'wishes/preferences'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: if I do not keep strict rules for myself, I will keep making mistakes and fail (understanding flexibility as risk)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: emphasizing the reasons for 'continuing to err if not strict' in a cautious, rational tone, weakening emotional expression, Interpreting around rules and consequences.

manifestations: constraining one's own Freedom of choice with absolute 'must/cannot' rules
treating one mistake as moral failure, Demanding flawless consistency of oneself
In social and work situations, shrinks choices and actions out of worry about making mistakes
outcomes: Concentration declines; work and online business affected

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: self-Demanding with 'I must never eat meat'
Treats the vegan community's norms as absolute standards

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: In social settings, excessively worrying about vegan-related mistakes
not yet discussing specific feelings with supportive family and friends, staying cautious

positive_force: Has clear values and moral motivation (vegan values)
having self-Reflection and Learning tendencies (actively researching and reminding oneself of values)
negative_force: repeatedly ruminating guilt and anxiety, affecting focus and daily functioning

target_behavior.behavior: persistent guilt and anxiety rumination, self-labeling with 'I am a terrible vegan'
antecedent: After accidentally eating meat at a gathering
When starting work or trying to focus
When thinking about one's own vegan rules and values
When entering social or dining settings
target_behavior.core_reason: Equates one mistake in all-or-nothing fashion with an overall moral failure, and maintains self-worth with rigid 'should / must' rules, leading to catastrophizing of mistakes and self-criticism
target_behavior.function: escaping unwelcome threats (erring again and moral failure), trying to gain control and maintain a pure self-image through harsh self-blame and monitoring
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased concentration, online business and Work affected;Daily rhythm disrupted;Impaired interpersonal interaction;Persistent anxiety and guilt
